title: Levels, ranks & achievements
items: Earn XP from your real activity (capped daily so it can't be farmed) to climb levels and ranks — Base Camp all the way to Peak.
40 achievements across training, nutrition, journaling, goals, gaming, supplements and social — track them on the new Progress page.
Show your rank and badges on your profile if you want (Settings → Profile sharing).

title: Friends & profile sharing
items: Find people by username, send and accept friend requests, and visit member profiles.
New per-section privacy controls (Settings → Profile sharing): choose Only me / Friends / Anyone for each area. Everything starts private, and your journal is never shareable.
Add a bio, and block anyone you'd rather not hear from. (Achievements, ranks and chat are coming next.)

title: Report card, editable history & more foods
items: New cross-system report card on Insights — an overall score with where you're winning and where to focus, across training, nutrition, gaming, mind, supplements and goals. Your dashboard now shows the score at a glance.
Edit past workouts (day, duration, notes, and every set) and journal entries (date, mood, body) in place — no more delete-and-redo.
Crop your profile photo to a square before it saves.
Food search now spans a curated fast-food set (Big Mac, Whopper, Chipotle…) plus the live USDA database of ~2M foods.

title: Valorant auto-sync
items: Add Valorant with your Riot ID (GameName#TAG) and it connects on the spot — region detected automatically.
Auto-imports recent Competitive matches as sessions (win/loss, agent, map, KDA, duration); re-syncing never duplicates.
Change your Riot ID anytime, and renames just work — sync follows your account, not your name.

title: Dota 2 auto-sync
items: Connect your Dota 2 account (via OpenDota — free, no API key) and import recent matches automatically.
Each match becomes a session with win/loss, KDA and duration; re-syncing never duplicates.
More games will follow as their official APIs allow.

title: Units & a Settings page
items: New Settings (under your profile menu) — choose Metric or Imperial, and weights show in kg or lb across the app.
Fixed: logging your first meal no longer asks for a date when one's already shown.

title: Workout builder fixes
items: Your custom reps now stick — picking a training goal no longer overwrites the reps you set on each exercise (it just sets the default for new ones).
The exercise search dropdown now closes once you pick one.

title: Set-by-set workout logging + personal records
items: Log every set — weight × reps — for each exercise in your day, not just a session title.
Your last numbers pre-fill so you can beat them, and personal records surface automatically.
Recent sessions now show exactly what you lifted.

title: Build your program, exercise by exercise
items: Every split day is now fully editable — add exercises from a searchable library or your own, set sets & reps, and edit or remove any of them.
Start a day from its suggested routine, then make it yours — works for the preset splits too.

title: Journal
items: A new private Journal tab — write a dated entry with a mood, your thoughts, and photos.
Photos are stored privately and only ever shown to you.

title: Workout goals, custom exercises & game logos
items: Workout day-guide: tap a goal (Strength / Muscle / Tone) and every exercise's reps retune to match — and it sticks.
Add your own exercises to any split day.
The gaming picker now shows real logos for popular games (Valorant, LoL, CS2, Fortnite), branded tiles for the rest.

title: Stay signed in + type your dates
items: The landing page now recognizes when you're already signed in — it shows 'Open dashboard' instead of making you log in again.
You can now type a date straight into any date field (MM/DD/YYYY), not only pick from the calendar.

title: Insights — patterns across everything
items: New Insights tab: 30- and 90-day stats plus a 12-week activity trend.
Cross-tracker findings a single app can't see — like whether your win rate is higher on days you train, or how training changes your appetite.
Opens from the sidebar or the dashboard's weekly summary.

title: Your data, your control
items: Export everything you've logged as a JSON file — Account → Data & account → Download.
Delete your account and all your data permanently, with a type-to-confirm step.

title: Install Upward on your phone
items: Upward is now an installable app — add it to your home screen for a full-screen, app-like experience (Share → Add to Home Screen on iPhone, or the install icon on Android/desktop).
Polished the mobile layout so controls clear notches and home bars.

title: A few fixes
items: The username checker now correctly flags a taken name before you save, not after.
Added a 'Post-workout' timing to the supplement tracker.
Fixed the supplement check-off flicker — one tap, one clean check.

title: Display names + username cooldown
items: You now have a display name you can change anytime — it's what shows around the app.
Your @username stays unique and can be changed once every 30 days.
Set both under Account.

title: Dashboard now shows goals & supplements
items: Your active goals appear on the dashboard with live progress bars.
A 'Supplements today' card shows how much of your daily stack you've taken.
The calendar now opens to the correct month for your timezone.

title: Fixed: dates now follow your timezone
items: Trackers were rolling over to the next day late at night — they ran on the server's clock (UTC), not yours.
Workout, meal, gaming, supplement and the dashboard now use your local day for 'today' and weekly stats.

title: Supplement tracker
items: Build your daily stack — name, dose, and when you take each one (morning, pre-workout, evening, anytime).
Tick supplements off as you take them; today's progress and your last 7 days show at a glance.
That completes every sidebar tracker — Workout, Gaming, Meal, Calendar, Goals, and Supplement are all live.

title: Goals
items: Set goals that are measurable (run 100 miles), streak-based (30 days straight), or simple done/not-done.
Add the 'why' behind each goal, an optional deadline with overdue & due-soon flags, and log check-ins that build a history.
Hit a rough week? Pause or adjust a goal instead of giving up. Reaching a target auto-completes it with a little celebration.

title: Smoother & faster
items: Charts now size themselves instantly — no more flicker or repeated console warnings.
Lighter background effects for noticeably smoother scrolling, especially on Brave.

title: Smarter targets, workout guides & more foods
items: Meal: choose a goal — lose, maintain, or gain — and your calorie & protein targets adjust to match.
Workout: every split now has a day-by-day exercise guide with sets, reps, and how to train for strength, size, or tone.
Added a 'Glute & Lower Focus' routine and ~55 more foods to the estimator.

title: Calendar
items: Plan your days with typed, checkable plans — workout, meal, gaming, goal, or other.
Everything you've tracked (workouts, meals, gaming) is overlaid right on the calendar.
Month view with a day panel to add, time, and tick off plans.

title: Update log, favorites & hardened security
items: Added this update log — tap the spark icon by your profile to see what's new.
Meals: save individual items as favorites (not just whole meals) and re-add them in a tap.
Consistent, themed date pickers across every tracker.
Tightened the site's Content-Security-Policy to a strict, nonce-based policy.

title: Meals got a lot smarter
items: Build a meal from multiple items with a built-in calorie & macro estimator.
Daily targets are auto-suggested from your profile and fully editable.
Today's totals and macros update live as you log.

title: Gaming tracker
items: Track multiple games, set daily/weekly goals, and log sessions.
See your win rate trend and matches by game.
Save a tracker.gg link for quick access (auto-sync coming later).

title: Dark mode & a live dashboard
items: New black-and-purple dark theme with a toggle (follows your system by default).
The dashboard now reads your real workout & gaming data.
A tailored weekly summary that reads like someone looked through everything.

title: Account & security
items: Set a unique username and a profile photo.
Two-factor authentication via an authenticator app.
Google & Discord sign-in, plus password reset.
